title: “Leave your country.”
paragraphs: “Leave your country.”

No map.
No GPS.
No pinned location.
Just a voice.
Genesis 12 says the Lord spoke to Abraham:
“Go from your country, your people and your father’s household to the land I will show you.”
Notice what God didn’t say.

He didn’t give coordinates.
He didn’t show the destination.
He didn’t explain the timeline.
Just one command:
Go.
Imagine the moment.

Family asking questions.
Neighbors whispering.
The road stretching into the unknown.
And Abraham packing everything…
Because when God speaks, faith moves before clarity arrives.
But here’s the deeper story.
Abraham’s journey wasn’t really about geography.
It was about trust.

Leaving comfort.
Leaving control.
Leaving the illusion that we can script our own future.
Because the life of faith always begins with surrender.
And this moment in Book of Genesis points forward to something greater.
Centuries later, God would send a promised descendant of Abraham:
Jesus Christ.
Through Him, the blessing promised in Genesis 12 reaches every nation.
Abraham walked into the unknown.
Jesus walked to the cross.
So that sinners like us could walk into grace.
Maybe God is whispering something to you right now.

Leave the habit.
Leave the secret sin.
Leave the life you built without Him.
Not because He wants to take life from you…
But because He’s leading you into promise.
Faith rarely begins with understanding.
It begins with obedience.
Would you follow God without knowing the destination?
Because sometimes the most powerful step of faith is simply this:
Take the first step.
